commits.subject: Support piped I/O when starting Seatbelt sandbox commands (#62350)
commits.reason: Keep upstream's macOS child owner so a future caller can use pipes while the sandbox keeps its network proxy alive. Preserve inherited streams and child exit status for the existing CLI.
evidence: The single changed source file at integration 34dc5bf533 matches upstream byte for byte. The existing Seatbelt entry point passes piped=false, awaits the same child and finishes denial logging. Linux and Windows retain the inherited-stream wrapper. The returned child owns the started proxy and keeps the existing kill-on-drop behavior.

On macOS, the preceding 0.12 development executable b8a4b5899 ran a real sandboxed command with a piped parent. Its stdin text reached stdout, its separate diagnostic reached stderr, and exit status 23 survived. Empty stdin delivered EOF to a second child which exited 0. This establishes the public inherited-stream behavior to preserve.

At official commit 60fcb1649f the only call of start_command_under_seatbelt selects inherited streams. The internal piped mode has no product caller at that commit. Verify the child handles and proxy lifetime through its first real caller when integrated.
